newsitem.title: USA: US Labor's Jackman says food, energy helped CPI.
newsitem.headline: US Labor's Jackman says food, energy helped CPI.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department economist Patrick Jackman said lower food and energy prices helped keep the overall U.S. Consumer Price Index low during the first three months of the year.
Jackman told Reuters Financial Television that the 0.1 percent rise in the March CPI was lower than what one would have expected and it was important to look at the trends over the past three months.

Jackman said that the CPI was running at an annual rate of 1.8 percent during the first quarter, much lower than the 3.3 percent rate of inflation for all of last year. But he said the lower CPI during the first quarter was due primarily to better price behavior for food and energy.
"The core (which excludes food and energy) is running essentially at what it was last year," he said.

Jackman a 4.5 percent increase in airline fares, due largely to reinstating a 10 percent federal tax on tickets, added about 0.1 percent to the CPI last month. Without that increase, the CPI would have been unchanged, he said.

"We have relatively low inflation at least by recent historical standards," Jackman said. He said increases in airline fares were offset by a drop in clothing prices and lower increases in housing costs.
"I think the factors more or less offset themselves this month," he said when asked about special factors at work in the report.
He did not see, as in recent past years, an undue amount of pressure on prices during the first four months of the year.
